memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: ""And I will make the Egyptians favourably disposed towards this people, so that when you leave you will not go empty-handed. Every woman is to ask her neighbour and any woman living in her house for articles of silver and gold and for clothing, which you will put on your sons and daughters. And so you will plunder the Egyptians."" - Exodus 3:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God says His people will not leave empty-handed. After generations of unpaid labour, they will walk out of Egypt carrying silver, gold and clothing — given willingly, because God will move Egyptian hearts.

This is not a promise of wealth to believers today, and we must not read it that way. It is God settling a specific historical account: centuries of stolen labour finally repaid. Interestingly, much of this gold would later be given to build the tabernacle — and some of it, tragically, to build a golden calf. God's provision can be worshipped or misused.

The lasting truth is about God's character. He is a God of justice who does not forget exploitation, and He is a God who provides for what He calls His people to do.

If you have been treated unjustly and there seems no way to recover what was taken, God has not lost the record. Vengeance and reckoning belong to Him (Rom 12:19), and He is never careless with His people.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I holding on to a wrong that I need to entrust to God's justice?
2. Do I use what God provides for His purposes or my own comfort?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Just and generous God, I trust You with what has been taken from me. Help me to use everything You give for Your glory. Amen.
